claim_text: The test suite is green (52 tests pass).
Fixture agent records 12 steps alternating llm_call/tool_call; replay-from-cache 0 LLM calls; substitution dirty-set 5 LLM re-execs; bisect 4 probes 0 LLM calls.
Record overhead per LLM call < 5 ms p99 (README §Performance targets).
The .sb HMAC chain detects tampering and Ed25519 verifier accepts untouched files (README §trace file format).
Trace size on disk < 30% of raw LLM payload bytes (CBOR + gzip + per-message dedup against header dictionary).
Repository layout matches README §Repository layout (planned): stepback/{recorder,replay,substitutions,trace,cli,tui}/ as packages, plus ts/, server/, examples/, docs/.
Each frame is a length-prefixed CBOR object (README §trace file format).
Replay of an unchanged 200-step trace from cache < 2 s end-to-end on a laptop, zero LLM calls.
Bisect of a 200-step trace ≤ 10 probes, ≤ 5 s wall, zero LLM calls.
Substitution of one step in a 200-step trace typically ≤ 10 real LLM re-executions (dirty-set size).
v0.1 target: Python SDK covering OpenAI + Anthropic clients and the LangChain tool registry.
Recorder shims for Anthropic / Bedrock / vLLM LLM clients.
Tool-registry shims for LangChain / CrewAI / AutoGen / MCP.
TypeScript SDK exists (ts/ directory).
Optional team-tier hosted replay engine (server/).
Five worked use-case examples in examples/ (01-bisect-bad-payment.md … 05-regulator-replay-under-new-policy.md).
Textual-based interactive TUI (`stepback inspect` interactive timeline + step viewer).
Web UI for the team tier.
`stepback verify --policy-changed-since` re-executes a trace under a newer toolwarden policy version and emits a structured report.
stepback depends on the same auditable-controller-core package toolwarden uses (shared verified append-only-log implementation).
stepback verify produces a signed Ed25519 attestation pack (regulator-replay tier, m8).
step_kind enumerates llm_call | tool_call | router | parallel_branch_open | parallel_branch_join | exception (parallel-branch + router step kinds).
nondeterminism_hash captures system clock reads, RNG draws, env vars, network responses as a divergence detector.
cost_usd is computed from usage × price-list version pinned in the trace header.
compare_branches produces a step-by-step diff: output diffs, decision changes, cost deltas, and which steps diverged from cache.
Cache hit rate for counterfactual policy audits is typically > 99%.

Pre-existing tools (LangSmith, LangFuse, Phoenix, Helicone, PromptLayer, TruLens, pytest-vcr, MS Agent Governance Toolkit, rr, Pernosco, airportyh/time-traveling-debugger, Sentry/Datadog APM) all fail the 'record + branch + substitute + cached partial replay' test (README §Why nothing else fills this gap).
trace_writer.py docstring: gzip+blob-dedup is the implementation of README's '<30% of raw LLM payload bytes' Performance target.
report.py docstring: 'deterministic and content-addressable so two engineers reading the same trace + substitutions get byte-identical reports' (rendered Markdown reports are byte-stable).
branch_io.py docstring: 'a counterfactual can never silently bind to a different recorded run' — load_branch raises BranchTraceMismatch on tampered traces.
shims.py docstring: wrap_openai / wrap_anthropic / wrap_langchain_tool / wrap_mcp_session are 'drop-in wrappers around the real client objects' usable in production by 'swapping one constructor'.
shims.py docstring: each wrap_* helper 'works against any object whose method shape matches the reference SDKs as of the dates pinned in stepback/pricing.py'.
report.py docstring: 'The CLI subcommand stepback report TRACE [--substitute SPEC ...] [--branch FILE] [--baseline-branch FILE] [-o OUT.md] is wired in stepback.cli'.

trace_writer.py docstring: 'A blob frame is only emitted when a given sub-tree is referenced at least DEFAULT_BLOB_MIN_REUSE times — otherwise the per-blob HMAC wrapper overhead (~280 bytes) would outweigh the saving.'
GROUNDING.md row 13: 'compressed .sb is 61.7% of raw payload bytes ... a large reduction (69.9%) vs the uncompressed .sb' — direct refutation of <30% target preserved as audit evidence.
stepback/pricing.py docstring claim that 'Prices … taken from published lists as of SNAPSHOT_DATE'.

Recorder.parallel() docstring: 'Sequential execution today; the on-disk frames are explicitly marked parallel so a future scheduler can re-execute branches concurrently without changing the trace shape.'

trace_writer.py docstring decomposition: 'gzip catches local redundancy inside one step, and the reuse-aware blob table catches cross-step duplication of recurring objects' — i.e. each compression mechanism is responsible for a distinct, measurable share of the saving.
shims.py: 'The Anthropic response shape is *canonicalised* into the OpenAI {"choices":[...],"usage":{...}} shape so cost accounting and replay semantics are uniform across providers.'
shims.py wrap_openai: returned OpenAIChatCompletion namespace mirrors SDK fields including 'choices[i].message.tool_calls' and 'choices[i].finish_reason' (not just .content / .usage).
shims.py: 'canonicalisation runs on both sides so a cache hit is bit-identical' — i.e. record-time canonical form == replay-time canonical form, byte-for-byte.

stepback/__init__.py exports add 15 new public symbols from shims (wrap_openai/anthropic/langchain_tool/langchain_tools/mcp_session, executors, wrapped classes) — the v0.1 public surface is now what the README §Status target line names.

pricing.py new public surface (aggregate_costs, check_budget, diff_costs, snapshot_age_days, BudgetCheck, format_usd, set_strict, MissingPriceError) is grounded by 31 test cases — but the docstring's 'Step-record contract' shape (specific keys step_id/step_kind/model/usage/cost_usd) has no schema-validation test pinning that records lacking these keys are 'silently treated as no-cost steps'.

Recorder.parallel() join inputs claim: 'a substitution inside any branch propagates dirtiness through the join (and only through the join — sibling branches stay cached).' The 'only through the join — sibling branches stay cached' half is not directly asserted by an existing test (test_branch_dirty_count_strictly_less_than_serial measures aggregate dirty count, not per-sibling cache state).

GROUNDING.md row 23: 'tests/test_e2e_replay.py gained 5 numeric-threshold tests pinning trace-size bounds, replay-vs-record wall-clock speedup, model-substitution cost drop > 1%, bisect probe-count <= ceil(log2 N)+1 (<=5 for the 12-step fixture), and a CLI bisect smoke.' — diff shows only 4 NEW tests in test_e2e_replay.py (HEAD~1 had 14 def test_, HEAD has 18); test_cli_bisect_finds_step pre-existed at HEAD~1 line 272 and is not new.

test_e2e_replay.py::test_replay_speedup_vs_record_is_measurable docstring: 'Cached replay must be measurably faster than fresh record. ... wall-clock under the recorder time'. The actual assertion is `replay_time < record_time * 2.0 + 0.05` which permits replay to be up to ~2x SLOWER than record (plus 50ms slack) — it cannot prove a speedup, only an upper bound on slowdown.

test_parallel_branches.py::test_zero_llm_replay_speedup_vs_record docstring: 'Cached replay must be measurably faster than fresh record... replay of an 11-step trace must take less wall-clock time than recording it.' Same shape as the e2e_replay twin: assertion `replay_time < record_time * 2.0 + 0.05` allows ~2x slowdown, not a speedup.

GROUNDING.md row 24: 'tests/test_parallel_branches.py ... replay wall-clock <= 2x record.' This row faithfully restates the assertion (which is what the test pins), but the language wraps the same speedup framing as row 23 — should be paired with a tightened test that actually shows replay < record before being treated as a speedup guarantee.

GROUNDING.md row 22: 'The full test suite is now green at 132 tests (up from 108 in row 11; +24 numeric-threshold guarantees added across compression, pricing, parallel-branches, e2e-replay, branch-io).' — pytest count 132 verified by command; per-file deltas e2e=+4, parallel=+6, compression=+3, pricing=+5, branch_io=+6 = +24 confirmed.

GROUNDING.md row 25: 'tests/test_compression.py grew 9 -> 12 tests, adding (a) blob-digest tamper detection independent of HMAC, (b) header advertises compression/blob_threshold/blob_min_reuse, (c) absolute-size ceiling: a 60-step chat-history compressed .sb is < 200 KB, uncompressed dominates compressed by >= 2x, per-step compressed cost < 3.5 KB.' Items (a) and (b) actually pre-existed in HEAD~1 (test_blob_digest_tamper_detection and test_header_advertises_compression_scheme were already in tests/test_compression.py); only the 60-step chat-history numeric-threshold test (and 2 others) are new in HEAD.

GROUNDING.md row 30: 'fan-out fixture ... records exactly 11 steps with kind counts llm_call=5, tool_call=4, parallel_branch_open=1, parallel_branch_join=1, and a ToolOutputSubstitution inside one branch dirties exactly 3 steps.' Verified: test_recorded_trace_numeric_bounds asserts those exact kind counts, and test_dirty_subtree_is_small_fraction asserts dirty == 3.

GROUNDING.md row 28: 'cached-prompt-token discount on gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 matches OpenAI's published 4x ratio.' Inline command output `ratio=4.000` matches; test_cached_token_savings_ratio_bounded pins [3.9, 5.0]. The CLAIM that this is OpenAI's published 4x ratio is grounded against the test value, but no citation URL to OpenAI's price page is committed alongside (so 'matches OpenAI's published' is asserted, not verified against an upstream artefact).

GROUNDING.md row 29: 'Bisect on the 12-step fixture finds the bad step in <= ceil(log2 12)+1 = 5 probes with zero LLM re-executions.' Bench output `bisect_probes=4 bisect_llm_calls=0 bad_step=step:12` matches; test_bisect_probe_count_is_logarithmic asserts the same upper bound. Grounded.

GROUNDING.md row 31: '.sbb branch files are tiny by construction: a single-substitution branch is between 50 B and 4 KB and < 50% of the base-trace size. Round-trip preserves count for all 5 substitution kinds.' Verified by test_sbb_branch_file_size_bounded + test_save_branch_substitution_count_matches_loaded.

GROUNDING.md row 32: 'trace-writer header now advertises the compression scheme metadata: compression == COMPRESSION_SCHEME (=gzip+dedup-2) and blob_threshold/blob_min_reuse are present in every .sb written with compression=True.' Inline reproducer command emits `compression=gzip+dedup-2 bt=200 bmr=2 expected=gzip+dedup-2 bt_def=200 bmr_def=2`. Grounded.
GROUNDING.md row 27: 'tests/test_branch_io_and_cli.py grew to 27 tests with 6 new numeric-threshold guarantees.' Verified per-file delta = +6 (HEAD~1 21 -> HEAD 27).

GROUNDING.md row 26: 'tests/test_pricing.py grew 26 -> 31 tests. Notable additions: cached-token discount bounded between 3.9x and 5.0x; diff_costs __total__ strictly equals sum of per-model deltas; RATE_TABLE/PRICE_LIST >= 10 entries and every alias resolves into RATE_TABLE.' All three additions match committed test bodies; per-file delta confirmed +5.

tests/test_e2e_replay.py::test_model_substitution_cost_drop_is_significant comment: 'mini is ~30x cheaper for the substituted step; even with only 1/6 LLM steps swapped the savings dwarf 1%.' The test only asserts `drop_ratio > 0.01` (>1%); the '~30x' multiplier and '1/6 LLM steps' framing are not pinned by any assertion or GROUNDING row that prints the actual per-model rate ratio for gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 vs the recorded baseline.
